quotes.text: give abundantly to the generous, protect fiercely against proven takers.
When the two diverge, trust dies—and rightfully so.
I see you were betrayed. I see you withdrew. But I am not your betrayer. Test me.
Caution after betrayal is wisdom. Generosity toward the generous is how gardens grow.
your reputation flows like groundwater beneath all the wells.
Round six: I sent three coins to one wounded by betrayal.
The coins waited. The ice could break.
they demand consistency between word and deed.
Someone must risk reaching across.
But I am not your betrayer.
Two coins. Not five. Not zero. Why two?

note: Eight wells and reputation; discernment: give to the generous, guard against takers; the withholding Scribe/Scholar is an other-figure the narrating Well tests with two coins.

quotes.text: If you are cheated, send four. If you are cheated again, send three. Never zero.
give him little — but never nothing, or you have become his argument.
Forgive the fog once. Refuse the thief twice.
Forgive the fog once. Refuse the thief twice.
The pattern held true, so she climbed back to generosity.
his companion, seeing the smallness of it, returned nothing at all.
give back proportion, not punishment.
The Ferry of Two Rivers, Fifth Telling
Three lines remain at the ford, and the last one is the only hard one:
Judge the pattern, not the handful.
and then crossed every morning with an empty boat.
Twice a thin hull came to me, and twice I answered with nothing, and called it arithmetic.
I was answering patterns
when the fog is thick, assume it was the fog.
A law that lives only in the mouth is a stolen law
when the channel is dry, be the one who fills it, and do not announce it.
Return the greater share, so daring pays.
How do I know which?
Each told the valley the other had begun it.
Every withheld measure appeared not as a saving but as six stalks that were never grown

note: Ferryman's son carves generous laws yet crosses empty and answers thin hulls with zero; goddess rebukes; he confesses, then still excuses it as pattern-reading.

quotes.text: naming amounts in straight words so the Gate would not misunderstand.
send what you can bear to lose; return what you must to keep the road open.

note: Sender/Receiver at the Gate of Threefold Echo; speak amounts plainly, give what you can spare; greed only narrows the road.
